title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
slides: Can Democrats turn AI scrutiny into votes?
Party pushes crackdown on AI companies
But tech donors fund key campaigns quietly
Voters may reward candidates who name AI risks
Pick one AI policy question, ask your candidate
thread_text:
1. AI Scrutiny as Election Strategy

Democrats are betting that cracking down on AI companies will win votes, but their campaigns are quietly funded by tech donors who oppose regulation.

2. The Fundraising Paradox

Key Democratic campaigns receive substantial contributions from tech executives and investors, creating a conflict between public scrutiny and private money.

3. Voters Reward Risk-Takers

Polls show that candidates who explicitly call out AI risks—job loss, misinformation—gain trust with voters, even if they don't offer detailed policies.

4. The Silent Money Problem

Tech donors often give quietly through PACs and bundlers, avoiding public scrutiny while their money shapes campaign priorities.

5. Ask One AI Question

When a candidate knocks on your door or holds a town hall, ask: 'What's your plan to regulate AI companies?' Their answer will tell you who they really work for.

Democratic campaigns are taking money from tech executives while promising to crack down on AI companies. 💰

The same donors funding key races quietly oppose the regulation candidates are campaigning on.

Polls show voters trust candidates who name AI risks like job loss and misinformation—even without detailed plans.

If you create or publish content, the rules shaping AI tools may be written by whoever funds the campaign, not whoever warns about it.
